title: Combination Sum II
statement: You get a list of positive integers, which may repeat, and a target. Find every different group of them that adds up to the target. Each number in the list can be used at most once. Do not return the same group twice.

example.caption: Using 1, 2, 2, 3 with target 4: the two 2s make one group, and 1 + 3 makes the other.

idea.sentence: Sort, then walk forward through the numbers. Skip a number equal to the one before it at the same depth, and stop the loop once a number is bigger than what is left.

jargon.plain: Make a choice, explore everything that follows, then undo the choice and try the next one.
Cutting off a branch early because it cannot lead to an answer. Here: once a number is too big, so is every number after it.

watch.inputHint: Two arguments: a list of positive numbers (repeats allowed), then the target, e.g. [1,2,2,3], 4

compare.bruteLabel: Check all 2^n subsets, dedupe the winners

rows.name: Brute force
rows.note: Try every subset, keep those with the right sum, and use a set to drop repeated groups.

rows.name: Sort, skip, prune
rows.note: Sorting costs n log n, which is small. The break on a too-big number and the skip of repeated values cut most branches in practice.

fast.takeaway: The worst case is still exponential, but pruning and the skip rule mean no group is built twice and many dead ends are never entered.

stages.title: Sort
stages.note: Sort a copy so equal numbers are neighbours and a too-big number means all later ones are too big.

stages.title: Choose
stages.note: Push sorted[i] and recurse from i + 1 with the smaller left, so each number is used once.

stages.title: Skip or stop
stages.note: Skip a number equal to its left neighbour at this depth. Break when a number is more than left.

stages.title: Record
stages.note: When left is exactly 0 the path adds up to the target. Save a copy.

stages.title: Undo
stages.note: Pop the choice after exploring it. Return all results at the end.

edges.title: No answer
edges.why: Only sums 2, 4 and 6 are possible. The search ends without ever recording.

edges.title: Use each number once
edges.why: Two separate 1s in the list may both be used. A single 1 could not be used twice.

edges.title: All equal
edges.why: Without the skip rule, the four choices of which three 1s would give four copies of the same group.

edges.title: Everything too big
edges.why: The first sorted number is already more than the target, so the loop breaks at once.

gotchas.text: Array.sort() with no argument sorts as strings, so 10 comes before 2. Pass (a, b) => a - b. Sort a copy, not the caller's list.
Save [...path], not path. The array is mutated after the save, so a stored reference would end up empty.
Save append([]int{}, path...), because slices share a backing array and a later append can overwrite a stored one. Also copy before sort.Ints, which sorts in place.
Skip with i > start, not i > 0. A repeated value is legal on a deeper level, where it extends the path (1 then 1).
break is safe here only because the list is sorted. In Combination Sum with unsorted numbers you must use continue.

recap.key: Sort. Loop from start. Skip a repeat of the previous value. Break when bigger than left. Recurse on i + 1.
recap.complexity: Time O(2ⁿ) worst case. Space O(n) for the recursion.
moves: Sort a copy of the candidates
Skip when i > start and sorted[i] == sorted[i - 1]
Push, recurse on (i + 1, left - sorted[i]), pop
